turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm finally replacing my old car and I've narrowed it down.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hear me out on all the options before you comment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The first one is a small used hatchback, five years old, cheap to run, with low mileage.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then there's a brand new hybrid sedan, really good on fuel, but it costs almost twice as much.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Option three is a used pickup truck, older and thirsty, but I could haul my bikes and furniture.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the last one is leasing an electric car for three years with a pretty low monthly payment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm done. What do you think?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If you mostly drive around town, the used hatchback gives you the most for your money. The hybrid makes sense if you do long commutes and plan to keep it for years. The pickup only pays off if you really haul stuff often.
